card: Restricts select socket exception monitoring to Windows and disconnects established P2P and HTTP connections on Windows if an exceptional condition occurs. Under poll, disconnects sockets with errors or hangups immediately when read readiness was not requested, preventing unrequested reads or doomed send attempts while receive backpressure is active. On non-Windows platforms using select, incoming TCP urgent data could leave exception sets continuously asserted and cause event loops to busy-spin. The change also ensures receive backpressure is preserved when errors occur on paused sockets. Comprehensive functional tests are added covering TCP urgent data, send stalls, and HTTP socket error paths.
evidence: Commit a626b28980 notes: 'select() can keep reporting a TCP urgent indication even when recv() has no data to read. P2P has no use for exceptional conditions on established connections, so disconnect to avoid a busy loop.'

Commit 628a74e299 notes: 'Disconnect directly on POLLERR/POLLHUP without read readiness, skipping the send attempt that would otherwise fail and disconnect the peer. This also changes the debug log message. Only call recv() for readable sockets.'

Commit 7cc5f0a901 notes: 'The select() backend only adds sockets to the exception set on Windows. Elsewhere, the set starts empty and remains empty after select(), so checking it with FD_ISSET() is a no-op.'
problem: TCP urgent data triggers an exceptional condition in select() that non-Windows platforms do not clear because out-of-band data is not consumed, risking a busy loop in the socket polling loop. Additionally, when receive backpressure pauses socket reads, poll() socket errors or hangups could trigger doomed send attempts or unrequested reads that bypass receive limits.

risk.why: Mistakes in socket event evaluation could prematurely disconnect healthy P2P peers or RPC connections, degrading node connectivity and remote command execution.

summary: Restricts socket exception monitoring in select() to Windows and immediately disconnects established P2P and HTTP connections on Windows when an exceptional condition is detected. For platforms using poll(), disconnects sockets with errors or hangups when read readiness was not requested, skipping failed send attempts and avoiding unrequested reads. Also adds test coverage for TCP urgent data, socket resets during send stalls, and HTTP socket errors.
